note: Authored fixtures, not run. Synthetic. Real overlap, 1/2/4-worker comparison, clean vs incremental output, out-of-order seeking, shared-font change, transition boundary edits, interrupted writes, disk exhaustion, pause/resume and late-worker rejection wait for Plan 14 and the user's explicit testing approval.

cases.title: Dependency readiness: only ready nodes run; user waits are real barriers; storyboard needs chosen Story+Look; scene builds need the approved storyboard
Useful parallelism: continuity groups, boundary contracts, a sting is one builder, workers grow only with evidence
Resource limits: separate pools, internal renderer workers accounted, pause and throttle block admission, no LLM polling
Lease fencing: only the current generation commits; a late stale worker is rejected and its log kept
Transitive keys: shared font and component changes reach every consumer; time changes reach neighbours; unknown dynamic dependencies are conservative
Atomic cache: private temp + commit marker, pins, in-use entries and disk limits
Boundary handles: transition overlaps, motion-blur shutter and global-time signals
Media assembly: one time base, verified frame counts, no blind concat, audio continuity, finish once
Fallback truth: slower paths are visible, never disguised; no instant success from an overlay
Measured throughput: evidence hooks record cold vs warm, critical path and failures, claim nothing
Slot failure and memory timeout: fail closed in the managed path, legacy behaviour unchanged elsewhere
Concurrent budget reservation: one remaining allowance, idempotent, unknown stays unknown
Bundle deadlock and stale owner: stable order, all or nothing, identity-based reclaim, fairness across films
Cache reuse is not approval; side effects are never replayed; reuse is explainable
